51596634.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant human RXR beta LBD (298 to 533 residues) expressed in Escherichia coli Rosetta assessed as dissociation constant by ITC method
51596634.references_previous: Reference 10: Chaikuaud, A.; Pollinger, J.; Rühl, M.; Ni, X.; Kilu, W.; Heering, J.; Merk, D. Comprehensive Set of Tertiary Complex Structures and Palmitic Acid Binding Provide Molecular Insights into Ligand Design for RXR Isoforms. Int. J. Mol. Sci. 2020, 21 (22), 8457.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Isothermal Titra: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were conducted on an Affinity ITC instrument (TA Instruments, New Castle, DE, USA) at 25 °C with a stirring rate of 75 rpm. RXRβ LBD protein (20 μM, prepared as described previously10) in buffer (20 mM Tris pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 5% glycerol) containing 3% DMSO was titrated with 33 (100 μM) in the same buffer containing 3% DMSO) in 26 injections (1 × 1 μL and 25 × 4 μL) with an injection interval of 150 s. As control experiment, 33 was titrated into the buffer and the buffer was titrated into the RXR LBD protein under otherwise identical conditions. The heat rate of the compound-RXR LBD titration was analyzed using Nano-Analyze software (TA Instruments) with an independent binding model.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption - part c: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) showed high-affinity binding of 33 to the RXRβ LBD (Kd = 0.03 μM). The fitting of the heat of binding is shown, and the isotherm at 25 °C is shown as inset.

assay_conditions.buffer_composition: 20 mM Tris, 100 mM NaCl, 5% glycerol, 3% DMSO
assay_conditions.control_method: Titration of ligand into buffer and buffer into protein under otherwise identical conditions
